disputed: The Trump campaign said at the time that the policies reflected long-held positions on 'energy dominance' and lower energy costs, not a transaction. The industry did not deliver the full $1 billion; the Senate report says 'hundreds of millions.' Estimates of total giving vary with methodology (Brennan counts at least $75 million to the campaign and PACs, while the Senate Democrats count $201 million). The donations were legal, and no official finding of an explicit quid pro quo exists. The Senate report is a partisan minority document.

items: April 11, 2024 dinner at Mar-a-Lago with roughly two dozen oil executives: Trump said $1 billion would be a 'deal' because of the taxation and regulation they would avoid, and pledged to reverse dozens of Biden environmental rules and freeze new ones. (Washington Post (https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2024/05/09/trump-oil-industry-campaign-money/))

In follow-up fundraisers in Houston and Dallas (May 22-23, 2024), Trump promised 'immediate approvals for energy infrastructure,' Arctic Refuge drilling, an end to the LNG export pause 'on the first day,' and revocation of California's Clean Air Act waiver. (Climate Power tracker (https://climatepower.us/research-and-polling/trump-promises-and-payments-tracker/))

House Oversight Democrats (Raskin) opened an inquiry into the dinner in May 2024 and later sent bicameral letters demanding documents from oil executives. (House Oversight Democrats (https://oversightdemocrats.house.gov/news/press-releases/ranking-member-raskin-probes-donald-trumps-offer-change-us-energy-policy))
sections.label: Documentation - the ask and the promises

items: A Senate Democratic report (Sept 24, 2026) found fossil-fuel donors put $201 million into Trump's reelection effort and $19 million into his inaugural fund. It also found the industry out-gave every other sector to Republican super PACs since 2021, by more than six times what healthcare gave. (Senate EPW Democrats (https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/press-releases-democratic?ID=D17E87C8-BA5B-4D3A-BA7A-CAD03C4B6F2D))

Kelcy Warren (Energy Transfer) gave $25 million to Trump's super PAC. The administration ended the Biden LNG export pause, clearing the way for Energy Transfer's LNG project, and Warren's wealth grew nearly 10% after the approval. (Brennan Center (https://www.brennancenter.org/our-work/analysis-opinion/fossil-fuel-industry-donors-see-major-returns-trumps-policies))

Harold Hamm's Continental Resources gave $1 million to MAGA Inc. (April 29, 2024). Occidental gave $1 million to the inaugural committee, and its CEO co-hosted a May 2024 fundraiser. (Climate Power (https://climatepower.us/research-and-polling/trump-promises-and-payments-tracker/); Brennan Center (https://www.brennancenter.org/our-work/analysis-opinion/fossil-fuel-industry-donors-see-major-returns-trumps-policies))

Global Witness also tallied about $19 million from fossil-fuel donors to the inaugural fund. (Global Witness (https://globalwitness.org/en/campaigns/fossil-fuels/fossil-fuel-donors-contributed-19-million-to-donald-trumps-inaugural-fund/))
sections.label: Documentation - the money

summary: At an April 2024 Mar-a-Lago dinner, Trump asked oil and gas executives to raise $1 billion for his campaign, calling it a 'deal' given the taxes and regulations they would avoid, and promised to reverse Biden-era environmental rules. The industry then became one of his largest funding sources.
title: The $1 billion ask: fossil-fuel money into Trump's campaign and inauguration
